conviction_note: The +10.8% 20-day run-up and the negative 25-delta skew (-2.33, calls bid, P/C OI 0.71) price a share-recovery-plus-M&A narrative that the only hard third-party data covering the actual quarter — IAA's own reported +11% unit volume for Apr-Jun and its CFO's 'broader industry volumes remain under pressure' — contradicts; I size that at roughly the name's own median historical reaction (-2.8%) rather than anything near the 4.76% implied, because Copart is a $31bn heavily-covered name with a genuine offsetting tailwind (record 23.3% total-loss frequency) and I found nothing extraordinary.

findings.finding: IAA/RB Global reported automotive unit volume of 658,800 lots, +11% year-over-year for Apr-Jun 2026 — two of the three months in Copart's fiscal Q4 — calling it the 'sixth consecutive quarter of outperforming the broader market,' with the CFO stating 'unit volume growth was supported by continued net market share gains, while broader industry volumes remain under pressure'; against a flat industry that arithmetic implies Copart's US insurance units were down roughly 5-7% in the quarter it is about to report, worse than the -4.2% it posted for Feb-Apr.
findings.why_not_priced: Copart's entire 20-day run-up window opens AFTER RB Global's 2026-08-04 print, and on 2026-09-03 the stock rose 4% on a JPMorgan upgrade whose stated thesis was that Copart 'appears to be picking up share in some states from an insurer' — the literal inverse of what the competitor reported for the same months. If the market had weighted IAA's own disclosed number you would see the 25-delta skew positive rather than -2.33, put/call open interest above rather than 0.71, and no 4% upgrade day into a name that has fallen after six of its last seven prints. The competitive story in the wire is generic ('IAA pressure'); the unpriced part is that the specific quarter being reported is one in which the competitor has already published its side of the ledger.
findings.independence: Copart's own last disclosure points the same way from a different document: Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-04-30) global insurance units -2.7% and US insurance units -4.2%, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260521385731/en/Copart-Reports-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Financial-Results (2026-05-21). Note the offset inside my own primary source, which is why the band reaches +0.5: the same RB Global transcript reports total-loss frequency up 90bp to a record 23.3% with 'leading indicators of the total loss frequency have improved modestly in recent months' — an industry tailwind for Copart assignments that I have deliberately not filed as a separate finding because it rests on the same document.

findings.finding: Copart is in a live, reported process to acquire CCC Intelligent Solutions (~$4.2bn equity value plus net debt), it upsized its revolver on 2026-01-23 to $1.25bn with a $500m incremental option explicitly permitting acquisitions, and on 2026-08-13 it seated David J. Berger — Wilson Sonsini's senior M&A-litigation and shareholder-activism partner — on the board, announced 2026-08-17, one day before the Bloomberg leak; the earnings call is a natural venue for a deal that would consume essentially all of the $4.2bn cash the current holder base owns this stock for.
findings.why_not_priced: CPRT rose across the window in which the CCC report broke, so the market is treating a possible $5bn+ cash-and-debt acquisition as free strategic optionality rather than as balance-sheet consumption. If it were pricing deal risk you would see puts bid into the print; instead the 25-delta skew is -2.33 with calls paid. No coverage I could find connects the Berger board seat, the January revolver upsizing and the CCC process as one sequence — each was reported as a standalone item. I size this small and with a wide two-sided band precisely because the announcement may not land on this call and because parts of the bull side (JPMorgan) read the deal as a positive.
findings.independence: Different document, same direction: the 2026-01-23 $1,250m unsecured revolver with a $500m incremental facility maturing 2031, sized and permitted for acquisitions and buybacks, replacing the 2021 BofA facility — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000119312526022730/d64083d8k.htm (filed 2026-01-26). The underlying deal report is Bloomberg, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-18/car-seller-copart-is-among-suitors-for-car-insurance-software-firm-ccc (2026-08-18). Caveat that cuts against me: Wilson Sonsini was already Copart's outside counsel before Berger joined the board, so the appointment is partly a formalization rather than a fresh signal.

searched_and_found_nothing: Jeff Liaw separation agreement as a hidden ASC 718 modification charge in the reported quarter — chased it properly and it is immaterial: the modified grants are 100,000 options (2021-03-09) and 175,000 options (2022-04-01) at a $106.31 exercise price with a $132.88 hurdle, i.e. 550,000 post-split options struck near $53.16 against a $32.13 spot, so eliminating the price goal has negligible incremental fair value; cash consideration totals only $900k. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000900075/000119312526286982/d70617dex101.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/900075/000090007522000052/cprt2022proxystatement.htm

Catastrophe activity in the May-July window as an assignment-volume swing factor — the sources contradict each other and give no vehicle-specific read: Swiss Re calls severe convective storm the leading H1 2026 insured peril at $28bn while Moody's titles its H1 review 'quieter and less costly'. https://www.swissre.com/institute/research/topics-and-risk-dialogues/climate-and-natural-catastrophe-risk/first-half-2026-insured-catastrophe-losses.html and https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/insights/insurance/united-states-severe-convective-storm-losses-quieter-and-less-costly-during-first-half-2026.html

Manheim ASP deceleration as a standalone finding — July 2026 MUVVI +1.3% YoY vs June's +2.1% (https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-july-2026-trends/, published 2026-08-07) looked like a lever failing, but IAA reported US insurance ASP +4% for the overlapping months and consensus already models only ~1.4% revenue growth, so it is priced and it is not what salvage ASP actually did
Interest income on the ~$4.2bn cash balance as an EPS swing — arithmetic makes it ~$0.008/share per quarter per 100bp, about 2% of the $0.39 consensus, too small to size
Copart careers/Workday job postings and yard-manager counts — 264 US openings on Glassdoor with no historical baseline to compare against, so the number carries no information

Insider transactions — no Form 4 purchases; aggregators show ~107,745 shares sold over three months and zero bought, including no purchase by the returning CEO, but no cluster or filing distinct enough to file as evidence
Any 8-K, pre-announcement or company disclosure between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-10 beyond the earnings-date press release
baseline_tension: Both findings cut against the baseline: the skew is negative (-2.33, upside paid) and the stock is +10.8% over 20 days, so the market is positioned long into a print where the competitor's own published volume data for the same months contradicts the upgrade thesis the last leg of that run-up rests on — and the run-up itself, on a name that has fallen after six of its last seven reports, is the exposure rather than the reassurance.
